facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Chapter 1 runs one night at Cutler Row, from the fourth division to the sixth; it is the same night the Ferriby tin was opened.
facts.quote: The same night, from the fourth division to the sixth.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi wrote her full four-part name (surname, generation character, given name, courtesy name) at the docket head in the lineage-hall hand; Wystan checked and blotted it; the name is never rendered on the page.
facts.quote: Surname, generation character, given name, courtesy name.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi is entered on the Register docket as assay of record, over Wystan's signature as Warden of Duty for the Night Register.
facts.quote: He wrote *assay of record* under her name, and under that his own, *W. Ashmore, Warden of Duty, for the Night Register*, and the division.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His hands tremor; the brass strike needed his elbow on the bench and his left hand pressed over his right.
facts.quote: He set his elbow on the bench and laid his left hand over the back of his right and pressed, and the tremor went down into the bench instead of into the seal.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: He has lived with the smell of brass wax for eleven years.
facts.quote: Resin came up off it, and under the resin a metal smell he had lived with for eleven years and still could not have named.

facts.subject: Brass wax
facts.fact: Brass wax is a dull yellow stick the Division issues only to its officers.
facts.quote: The Register's wax came out of the forms drawer: brass wax, a dull yellow stick the Division issued to its officers and to nobody else.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: The wedge's crown shows a quarter inch of new growth inside the sealed chapter tin, logged in the day-book margin as 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'.
facts.quote: The number was already in ink in the margin, *crown +¼ in sealed, 11d*, and the same eye an hour later would only give him the same number with less sleep behind it.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: The growth continued inside a Fixatio tin whose seal was whole; Wystan recorded that in the day book.
facts.quote: Something in the tin had gone on running under a seal that was sold to the courts as a promise that nothing would.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: Chain of custody: Tally cut the wedge in the North Ferriby cut; Yinzhi sealed it there under chapter wax on the 9th; the chapter's tin was found whole; its seal was broken at Cutler Row by the assay in the officer's presence.
facts.quote: Cut in the cut by Tally, N., and sealed there by the assay under chapter wax, the 9th.

facts.subject: Ferriby wedge
facts.fact: The wedge was moved by gloved forceps into a fresh Division Fixatio tin, sealed with brass wax and struck with Wystan's brass: Register file Ferriby, exhibit one.
facts.quote: Contents moved by forceps, gloved, to a Division tin; brass wax; struck.

facts.subject: Chapter's tin
facts.fact: The chapter's emptied tin was left unwashed, upright at the far end of the scullery sill.
facts.quote: He stood it upright at the far end of the sill, away from the wash-tray, where nobody could put it in the vinegar by mistake.

facts.subject: Ferriby tin
facts.fact: Wystan holds that the exhibit is no longer the Society's; the chapter may ask the Division in writing and will be refused.
facts.quote: From this division it is not the Society's.

facts.subject: Chapter wax
facts.fact: Four pieces of the broken chapter seal (two from the front-room blotter, two from under the desk) fit the join; folded in a druggist's paper, labelled and dated, laid on the sill beside the tin.
facts.quote: He wrote on the outside, *Chapter wax, Timberline. Broken by the assay at Cutler Row in the officer's presence. Four pieces.*

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: A taste of green from the wedge stays at the back of his tongue through three rinses and grounding tea; he does not record it. Unresolved.
facts.quote: He had nothing to put against that. He did not write it down.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Appearance: tall and narrow, hair tied at the nape and hanging to the waist, dark red in lamplight, a white line through the left eyebrow.
facts.quote: The black glass gave him back a tall, narrow man with his hair tied at the nape and hanging to the waist, dark red where the lamp caught it, and a white line through the left eyebrow.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: LIE: Yinzhi tells Wystan her bracelet stopped pulling at the sink. It did not (her thumb is on the badly struck mark as she says it). Uncorrected; Wystan believes it.
facts.quote: It went quiet when you were at the sink.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: Tally's insert was dated the 14th and is held open at the Night Register.
facts.quote: Your insert of the 14th has been read at the Night Register and is open here.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: Wystan's letter asks Tally to rewalk the line as before the 11th, measure the same way and log each find at the time in a notebook kept on his person: a second dataset from the same observer.
facts.quote: I want a second dataset from the same observer.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: The letter asks who set the parish marker on the Ferriby line and when, and what the animals drank or licked from.
facts.quote: Tell me what the animals on that line put their mouths to: water, licks, troughs, anything that is set out and filled.

facts.subject: Letter to Tally
facts.fact: The letter is signed 'Night Register, Cutler Row' under brass wax and goes with the Society's bag in the morning bundle; the nine-word wire was rejected.
facts.quote: He signed it *Night Register, Cutler Row*, dropped a thumb of brass wax beside it, and set the brass in the wax.

facts.subject: Night Register
facts.fact: The Night Register has been one officer for four years, in a scullery on Cutler Row whose main goes off at the eleventh division; a Prime Warden's minute could fold it.
facts.quote: It had been true for four years, since the Division wanted a particular officer somewhere else and found him a scullery on Cutler Row with a main that went off at the eleventh division.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi was eight months capped and burned two coils.
facts.quote: If it comes to a hearing, and it will not come soon, somebody will stand up and say the assay was eight months capped and burned two coils and cannot say what she read.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Wystan sends Yinzhi home; she may tell the chapter the tin is under his brass at Cutler Row and they may write.
facts.quote: Tell them it is under my brass at Cutler Row and they may write.

facts.subject: Qiu Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi knows Wystan counts forty-two minutes, and tells him to eat something at the sixth.
facts.quote: "Then you counted."

facts.subject: Ferriby site
facts.fact: Eleven hinds and a stag died inside a quarter mile, the last twenty-two paces short of the parish boundary marker; clean ground beyond, checked twice by Tally.
facts.quote: The last of them twenty-two paces short of the parish boundary marker.

facts.subject: Ferriby site
facts.fact: Four ravens in the birch would not come down to the carcasses.
facts.quote: Four ravens in the birch that would not come down.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His Register position, written in the day book under 'edges': a dose goes where it is put. (Held as true by him; see the misreading.)
facts.quote: A dose goes where it is put.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: MISREADING: Wystan concludes the formulator's dose stops where it was put, so every site will show a hard edge. True of Ferriby's first site only; false of every dose after.
facts.quote: Whatever the formulator had put into those animals had stopped where he stopped putting it, because a man who works at a distance from his own work has to choose the distance, and every site in the four counties would show the same hard margin once somebody walked it with a rule.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: The Ferriby hind is the forty-second minute in the back of his day book.
facts.quote: At the back of the book, on the pages he kept for them, he entered the forty-second minute beneath the other forty-one.

facts.subject: Cutler Row
facts.fact: The main came back on at the sixth division; Wystan logged 'main on, 6th'.
facts.quote: The main came back at the sixth division.

facts.subject: Day desk
facts.fact: The Division's day desk is at the front of the same Cutler Row building, up four steps from the passage.
facts.quote: He lifted it the way he lifted everything, two fingers and a thumb at the rim of the lid and the base, and he took the docket form in the other hand, and he went out through the front room and along the passage, where the hum ran under the boards the whole length of the house, and up the four steps to the front of the building where the Division kept its day desk.

facts.subject: Brack
facts.fact: The docket book's Ferriby entry carries Brack's Bureau return: Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, tertiary expression, no operator indicated, no file; ruled off in red and marked closed.
facts.quote: Two lines had been ruled under it in red.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan's memorandum opens Register file Ferriby under the red rule, does not dispute the measurement, and puts 'edges' in the margin by Brack's line; the docket form is folded in at the page.
facts.quote: In the margin, level with Brack's line, he wrote one word.

facts.subject: Day clerk
facts.fact: An unnamed day clerk (about fifty, bald crown with grey fringe, wen by the nose, brown coat buttoned wrong, black sateen oversleeves) reads only Brack's line, calls it closed and shelves the book unread.
facts.quote: He shut the book over the memorandum, over the folded docket and the one word in the margin, took it off the lectern in both arms and slid it into its place on the shelf behind the counter, spine out.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: At the end of the night the Ferriby tin sits on the scullery sill beside the chapter-wax fold, with his brass lying on the lid.
facts.quote: Wystan picked up the tin by its rim, two fingers and a thumb, and carried it back down the passage over the hum to the sill, and set it beside the fold of chapter wax, and laid his brass on the lid.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Chapter runs Day 1 from noon to the ninth division.
facts.quote: He woke at noon with the shutters closed and the house humming under him.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His hands shake with a fine fast tremor at waking, worse in the right; the Division filed it as a disciplinary observation.
facts.quote: The Division had entered it in his file under a different heading, in the copying hand, as a disciplinary observation.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Holding himself suppressed asleep leaves his jaw and shoulders aching each morning.
facts.quote: He had kept himself down all night, asleep, the way he kept himself down awake, and this was what it came to in the mornings.

facts.subject: Keld's minute
facts.fact: Keld's minute is held by Wystan and checked each morning against a written record; the minute first, then the paper.
facts.quote: The minute came first and the paper after, because a record read first is a record remembered, and after that the minute would only agree with it.

facts.subject: Keld's minute
facts.fact: The written record's exact text, in brown ink gone tea-coloured, folded in four in Wystan's coat.
facts.quote: *Keld, O. Door on the landing. Handle iron, cold. Right hand. Lamp behind. Count at thirty-one. Legs tired. Not afraid. Bread, dark, butter. Says: "Sixth. They said the sixth. Hold it to the sixth."*

facts.subject: Keld's minute
facts.fact: On Day 1 the minute matched the record exactly, forward and backward.
facts.quote: It had not moved.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan was the second man through the landing door and took the minute off the handle; the relief came late.
facts.quote: The first had his arms full, so it was Wystan who put his hand on the handle, and that was how he had the minute.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: His brass token was left on the tin lid at Cutler Row at the sixth division; he went to the medical house without it.
facts.quote: His brass was lying on a tin lid on Cutler Row, where he had left it at the sixth division, and he gave his name at the porter's hatch with nothing in his hand.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: He retrieved the brass from the tin lid and put it in his waistcoat.
facts.quote: He put it in his waistcoat.

facts.subject: Brass token
facts.fact: The Register's token is brass because the Night Register is not a full desk; carried four years, never asked to change it.
facts.quote: He had carried it four years and had never asked to have it changed.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld's Division coat hangs on a peg in his room with his silver token still in it.
facts.quote: Nobody had ever come to take it back.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld lives in the upper-floor end room of the Division medical house, two streets over behind the stables.
facts.quote: Keld's room was on the upper floor at the end.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld counts under his breath to varying numbers (twelve, nineteen, seven, four, thirty); Wystan cannot find what he counts.
facts.quote: He could find nothing in the street that Keld was counting.

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld asks for 'them' and repeats 'They said the sixth'; the orderly says he asks twice, same as always.
facts.quote: "Twice. Same as always."

facts.subject: Keld
facts.fact: Keld taught Wystan the druggist's fold in the back room of the old office on the river.
facts.quote: Keld had taught him to fold a paper the druggist's way.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Six people alive know what Stage Wystan holds; Keld knew first but is not counted among the six.
facts.quote: Keld was alive.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle is one of the six who know his Stage; she had it off his file the week he was put on nights.
facts.quote: She had had it off his file the week he was put on nights, and she had read it, and had said nothing then, and had said nothing since.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle, about sixty, the only person in the building who calls him 'Warden of Duty'.
facts.quote: She was the only person in the building who used the title, and she used it as other people use a surname in a quarrel.

facts.subject: Night Register file
facts.fact: The Register may keep the file open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing and not a day longer; entered in Lyle's minute in ink under her silver seal, initialled by Wystan.
facts.quote: *The Register may keep this curiosity open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing, and not a day longer. E. Lyle, Prime Warden.*

facts.subject: Night Register file
facts.fact: The Register's position, copied into Lyle's minute: a dose goes where it is put, and every site will show the same margin.
facts.quote: The Register's position is that a dose goes where it is put, and that every site will show the same margin when somebody walks it with a rule.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan initialled both position and term; his hand shook on the second initial.
facts.quote: His hand shook on the second initial and he did not stop to steady it.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Lyle signs the northern office's quarterly return together with the gauge-housing seal on inspection day.
facts.quote: At the inspection the Board's man reads my housing and seals it, and the northern office's return goes up the same day under the same seal, and I sign the two together.

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: Lyle refuses to put the Night Register on the return quarrelling with the Bureau.
facts.quote: "I will not put the Night Register on that return quarrelling with the Bureau over deer."

facts.subject: Day clerk
facts.fact: The day clerk heard 'eleven hinds and a stag' and wrote something in his ledger.
facts.quote: She said it back to him quite flatly, and the clerk at the end of the counter wrote something very small in his ledger.

facts.subject: Edwyn Brack
facts.fact: Edwyn Brack, Bureau, about fifty, coil-burn scar on right thumb; had seen the memorandum.
facts.quote: "I have seen your memorandum."

facts.subject: Edwyn Brack
facts.fact: Brack stands by his classification: bleed, Verdantia, tertiary, no operator.
facts.quote: It's bleed. My man took it off a calibrated coil against the standard and it's bleed, Verdantia, tertiary, and there's no operator in it.

facts.subject: Bureau field sheets
facts.fact: Brack gave Wystan the Bureau's raw Ferriby field sheets with coil calibration, in a green-taped folder, unasked.
facts.quote: "No. Master Brack gave them to me in the passage."

facts.subject: Bureau field sheets
facts.fact: Lyle orders the sheets entered as received unasked, today, before he reads them.
facts.quote: "Then enter them as received unasked, today, with the division, before you read a line of them."

facts.subject: Elspeth Lyle
facts.fact: LIE: Lyle says she did not send for Brack (she did; tell: the pen did not stop, eyes on the green tape). Uncorrected.
facts.quote: "I did not send for Master Brack."

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: MISREADING: Wystan believes the residue settling in a shut room falls on everyone alike; in fact it runs to him (H13).
facts.quote: It was what any shut room did by this hour, with the main running under it and people at work in it all day, and it came down on everybody in the room alike; Lyle had simply never sat a night on the Register, and had nothing on her hands to feel it with.

facts.subject: Edwyn Brack
facts.fact: Brack heard Wystan say he will get a hand and not a purse.
facts.quote: "I will get a hand and not a purse."

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: Chapter 2 runs one night at the Greyshaft Nine coldhouse, the second division to the ninth; it is the twelfth day Vesk has watched Malphas (eleven days, the twelfth begun at the second division).
facts.quote: The twelfth had started at the second division and he had never asked.

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: The main under Greyshaft Nine has been capped four years; the standpipe housings on the west wall are dead, there is no meter and no bill; the row was struck off the Board's schedule.
facts.quote: The main under Greyshaft Nine had been capped four years, and the standpipe housings along the west wall stood there in their brackets with nothing in them, iron gone the colour of an old kettle, capped and unbilled and quietly rusting into the slate.

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: The drip in the coldhouse's far corner runs twenty-two drops a minute; Vesk counted it a year ago and still counts it.
facts.quote: Twenty-two drops a minute.

facts.subject: Greyshaft Nine
facts.fact: The housing gauge reads four degrees in the coldhouse.
facts.quote: What there was instead was the one thing Vesk could not get past: the Lord had been sitting on an iron bench in a room the housing gauge had at four degrees since the first division, with no gloves on and his coat folded beside him and not under him, and his fingers were the colour of a living man's fingers.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: The ninth hind, eleven days under the ferment, is structurally liquid and cellularly whole; Nuvalik moves her off the rail onto the slate table at the second division.
facts.quote: Eleven days of the ferment had taken the connective net out of her and left the meat where it was.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: Nine carcasses hang on the rail, eleven days, no smell; the crown growth stands nine inches at best.
facts.quote: Eleven days on the rail and no smell and nine carcasses signed by nobody, and it had been beautiful work and it had been an argument about what a thing is.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk built the contractile matrix into the third-dilution formulation on one pour (in since the eleventh hour, stood just under an hour).
facts.quote: Into it, at the dilution, so that the thing that grew and the thing that pulled came off the same pour and arrived in the same tissue at the same time.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk has gone four days without sleep.
facts.quote: That was the whole of the last four days and he had not slept through any of them.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk's hands close only two thirds of the way; he carries anything in both flat palms.
facts.quote: He looked at his hands on the bench and made them close, and they got two thirds of the way and stopped.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Two grafts on Vesk's hand: the first clean, the second holds but grips badly; its two fingers grow ridged yellow nails he cuts every fourth day and hides from the lamp.
facts.quote: The second had taken in the way that a thing takes when it has been asked twice, which was well enough for holding and badly for gripping, and the nails on the two fingers that took had come in ridged and yellow and had never stopped growing since.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk's home village laid flat beck stones on graves, one a year for nine years, until the ground was finished.
facts.quote: Flat ones, out of the beck, one a year for nine years, until the nine were on and the ground was finished.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Malphas calls Foss by his given name, Ilmar.
facts.quote: "Ilmar," Malphas said.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss has the gauge-housing open, its seal broken on a quarterly inspection that stopped coming nine years ago.
facts.quote: He had the coil out again, in pieces, the jeweller's glass screwed into his eye, and the brass of the gauge-housing open beside him with the slate back off it and the seal broken on a quarterly inspection that had stopped coming nine years ago.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas wants the Arbitration Division's Warden-of-Duty field manual for its unsigned attribution paragraph; he has designed against it for two years from hearsay.
facts.quote: The manual has a section on attribution and the section has a paragraph in it that nobody signed, and every officer who works a residue works it off that paragraph, and I have never read the paragraph, and I have been designing against it for two years out of what other people tell me is in it.

facts.subject: Arbitration Division field manual
facts.fact: The field manual is a numbered issue logged against a name in an issue book and surrendered when an officer is struck off, dies or goes to the Bench.
facts.quote: It is a numbered issue.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss held a numbered instrument for eleven years; when struck they took the instrument before the oath.
facts.quote: I had a numbered instrument off the same kind of book for eleven years and the day they struck me they wanted the instrument before they wanted the oath back.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss refuses to wire for the manual: a wire is nine words and the flimsy is kept at both ends for a turn of fourteen days.
facts.quote: A wire is nine words.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss will ask men in turn for a copy of the manual; it will take a season, and Malphas accepts a season.
facts.quote: It will be a season.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Malphas told Vesk the fourth hind's shoulder gave contraction twice; Vesk has had nothing like it from the others.
facts.quote: The Lord said contraction.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: LIE: Nuvalik tells Vesk everything the fourth hind gave her is written down. It is not: she got contraction twice and did not record it (tell: blade wiped on the apron first). Uncorrected (H08).
facts.quote: Everything the fourth hind gave me is written down.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik's tell: she wipes the blade on her apron before she speaks; it frightens Vesk.
facts.quote: She wiped the blade on her apron before she spoke, which was the one thing about her that frightened him, and it did not frighten him less for happening every day.

facts.subject: the book
facts.fact: The cell's book is kept on the shelf over the ice press, kept by Nuvalik since the first night; nobody else has taken it down.
facts.quote: It is on the shelf over the press where it has been since the first night and nobody has taken it down but me.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik's name was worn by three people before her; she says she has spent all three of hers in this room.
facts.quote: The name I wear was worn by three people before me.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: The pour: four places along the near flank, not the wound, a count of forty between each; the colour cleared inland, faster at the two forward pours.
facts.quote: He worked it in at four places along the near flank, a little at each, and between each he stopped and gave it the count of forty and watched the colour go out of the surface as the channels took it away inland.

facts.subject: Ilmar Foss
facts.fact: Foss, at the glass, calls the synthesis filthy and correct and wants both findings in the book.
facts.quote: It is filthy, and it is correct, and those are two separate findings and I want both in the book.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas's hands keep a living man's colour after sitting ungloved on an iron bench at four degrees since the first division (H07).
facts.quote: What there was instead was the one thing Vesk could not get past: the Lord had been sitting on an iron bench in a room the housing gauge had at four degrees since the first division, with no gloves on and his coat folded beside him and not under him, and his fingers were the colour of a living man's fingers.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: MISREADING: Vesk believes the ice press's warm air along the east wall explains why Malphas's hands never take the cold (worked out the fourth night, never said). Never corrected; never paid as recognition.
facts.quote: The press threw its warm air along the east wall and the gauge bench stood in the middle of it, and that was the whole of why the Lord's hands never took the cold.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: Nuvalik states the hind: no Crystal, no self, a net that shortens toward the emptier end.
facts.quote: She is meat with a new net in it and the net can shorten.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: No anchor in the hind and there will not be one (an anchor is a binding, a binding takes a name); she cannot be told where to go, only given somewhere emptier.
facts.quote: Four to six without an anchor, and there is no anchor in her, and there will not be one.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk claims she needs only eleven feet since the building is the emptiest place in four streets; Malphas answers she has not yet got up.
facts.quote: Then she will not need four days.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas orders the night written up in the book, in ink, with the division, under the project's name, by four hands.
facts.quote: I want the whole of this project written down under the name I gave it, by four hands, in one book, because the file somebody builds out of us will be built off what is written and I would rather it be built off this than off a clerk's recollection of it.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: The hind does not stand. The hide at her shoulder draws up once, a hand's breadth, untouched; Vesk tells nobody and does not call Foss's glass to it.
facts.quote: He did not call Foss back to put the glass on it.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk ends the night writing the division in the book's margin.
facts.quote: Then he went to the shelf for the book and wrote the division in the margin.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Day 2, fourth division: Deming enters the second tranche of the Swale supply in the Swale book's wastage column, in his own hand, in figures and in words.
facts.quote: The second tranche went out of the Swale book at the fourth division, in Deming's hand, in the wastage column.

facts.subject: the Swale book
facts.fact: Four years of wastage at the array ran flat quarter by quarter; this quarter the first tranche (small) and the second make a step in the column.
facts.quote: The column went down the page without a step in it anywhere.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming has kept the Swale page himself for three of its four years.
facts.quote: He had kept this page himself for three of those years.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas sent for Deming to the coldhouse after the ninth division (the work already named) and ordered the Project name onto the letter; Deming argued against it with the precedent, and Malphas answered only 'I would prefer the file be built off a word I chose.'
facts.quote: He had sent for him to the coldhouse after the ninth division, when the work already had its name, and told him there, while Deming stood by the door with his hat in his hands and the rain on his shoulders and argued.

facts.subject: the covering letter
facts.fact: The Xu covering letter to the Logistics factor names the account as Project Zombification, second tranche, in Deming's copying hand.
facts.quote: On the account of Project Zombification, second tranche.

facts.subject: the covering letter
facts.fact: The letter names Verdantia: the second tranche drawn down as wastage for loss at the array housings.
facts.quote: The second tranche of Verdantia under the Swale supply contract drawn down against it as wastage and entered this day in the house's book.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming gives the cause of the loss as the thaw; this is his own false cover, in the letter and aloud ('What keepers say in a thaw').
facts.quote: Cause: the thaw.

facts.subject: the covering letter
facts.fact: Deming signs the letter for the house and presses the Xu chop under the signature in red paste.
facts.quote: He wrote the house's compliments, and signed for the house, and pressed the chop beneath the signature in red paste out of the lacquer box, rocking it once each way so the corners took.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming privately counts thirty-one days left of his usefulness to Malphas (counted on the house almanac).
facts.quote: Thirty-one days of a man who held the contract, and the pen, and the chop, and was useful.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming knows Malphas counted the thirty-one days before he did and let him argue anyway.
facts.quote: Malphas had counted them already.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: From the house's own copies of old returns, Deming derives eleven weeks from the factor taking the page to the published Logistics return coming back down the river.
facts.quote: It came out at eleven weeks.

facts.subject: the Logistics factor
facts.fact: The Logistics factor stays unnamed; Deming knows his name and has never used it; the house calls him the factor.
facts.quote: Deming had known his name for years and had never once used it.

facts.subject: the Xu house
facts.fact: The Xu counting house is still on the main; per the factor, half the Swale is off it.
facts.quote: Half the Swale's off it.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming tells the factor the carters' notes are clean and every cart up the Swale road this quarter went full (true).
facts.quote: Every cart that went up the Swale road this quarter went up full and was entered full.

facts.subject: the Logistics factor
facts.fact: The factor pushes to move the loss into carriage on the house's bond; Deming holds it to wastage and the factor accepts it on his word.
facts.quote: Wastage. On your word.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming tells the factor that in eleven weeks the capital will see a bad spring on the Swale line, and asks for it noted.
facts.quote: In eleven weeks somebody in a room in the capital will look at the Swale line and see a bad spring.

facts.subject: the factor's pocket-book
facts.fact: The factor writes Deming's words, with the division, in his black oilcloth pocket-book.
facts.quote: 'Xu says bad spring. Swale. Fifth division.'

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming concludes the factor is a carriage man who lost interest in the Swale page once carriage was lost to him. Not true: do not treat as fact.
facts.quote: Once the carriage was lost to him, the Swale page was the capital's trouble and no longer his.

facts.subject: the covering letter
facts.fact: The factor reads the second line twice and makes a small hooked mark in the margin beside it: neither his query cross nor his initial; Deming has never seen it. Uninterpreted.
facts.quote: A short downstroke with a hook at the foot of it, turned to the left.

facts.subject: the Logistics factor
facts.fact: The quarter's returns, with the house's Swale page, go into the front of the factor's satchel in a string bundle.
facts.quote: The quarter's returns went in at the front, the house's Swale page with them, in a bundle with a string round it that he tied off with his teeth and one hand.

facts.subject: the covering letter
facts.fact: The letter goes apart from the returns, into a flat folder between two boards at the back of the factor's satchel.
facts.quote: It went into the back of the satchel, into a flat folder between two boards, and the boards were pressed shut on it and the strap buckled over.

facts.subject: the Logistics factor
facts.fact: The factor's lie: covering letters go in the stove at quarter-day. The letter was filed flat between boards; his 'I've still got a...' self-repairs to 'Stove had it.' Do not treat as true.
facts.quote: Covering letters stop on my desk and go in the stove at quarter-day.

facts.subject: Deming
facts.fact: Deming tells the Hollow Shaft story aloud to the factor, as a joke about careless men.
facts.quote: That is how they found the Hollow Shaft people.

facts.subject: the Hollow Shaft precedent
facts.fact: Hollow Shaft, twenty years ago: a cell; the hand was never found; the payer was found by one name in a private letter and amerced to his means.
facts.quote: They never found the hand, the one that did the work, never found him at all.

facts.subject: the Logistics factor
facts.fact: If the Division wants Xu, it will wire: 'Xu, Swale, explain.'
facts.quote: Nine words.

facts.subject: the Logistics factor
facts.fact: The factor leaves upriver on foot along the river road with the satchel (and the letter), not looking back.
facts.quote: The factor came out below onto the river road and turned upstream along it, stooping, with the satchel against his hip and one mitt resting on the flap.

facts.subject: Day 2
facts.fact: The chapter runs Day 2 from the fourth to the sixth division.
facts.quote: Down the river the bell began on the sixth division.

facts.subject: the blotter
facts.fact: The blotter on the low table by the stove carries the letter's second line in reverse, in Deming's copying hand.
facts.quote: The second line was there, pale blue and backwards, in the house's best copying hand, which was his.

facts.subject: Day 4 to Day 5
facts.fact: The chapter runs from Day 4, sixth division, at Cutler Row to Day 5, sixth division, at the Ferriby cut.
facts.quote: *Cutler Row, then the North Ferriby cut and the parish marker. Day 4, the sixth division, to Day 5, the sixth.*

facts.subject: Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi knocks once and enters Cutler Row without waiting for the first time.
facts.quote: She had not done that before.

facts.subject: the parish marker
facts.fact: Per Tally's letter, the marker is the Ferriby estate's old survey stone, the corner of their ground, set by the estate before the parish was on the roll; the parish adopted it as its bound afterwards; nobody knows who cut it or when.
facts.quote: It is the Ferriby estate's old survey stone, the corner of their ground, set by the estate before the parish was on the roll.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: Tally is walking his line every day since Wystan's letter, the same way, writing it at the time, and is at the stone most days at dusk writing up.
facts.quote: I am walking again, every day since, the same way as before, and writing it at the time like you said.

facts.subject: Tally's letter
facts.fact: Tally's letter answers who set the marker but not Wystan's second question (what the animals drank from).
facts.quote: He had asked two things. Tally had answered one.

facts.subject: the day book
facts.fact: Wystan's day-book margin now reads: edges / ask Tally who set the marker / the estate. before the roll. / the round.
facts.quote: Beneath *edges* and *ask Tally who set the marker* and *the estate. before the roll.* he wrote two words.

facts.subject: the hacks
facts.fact: The two Division hacks were hired on a chit to the northern office and go on the Prime Warden's bill with the three lamps.
facts.quote: The Division's stables stood behind the medical house, and the ostler gave them two hacks on a chit to the northern office, which put the hire on the Prime Warden's bill with his three lamps.

facts.subject: the Timberline bench
facts.fact: Wystan wires the Timberline bench (nine words) that the assay of record is with the Register at Ferriby, returning tomorrow.
facts.quote: *Assay of record with Register at Ferriby. Returns tomorrow.*

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan had not slept since the noon before the ride; he rides badly, Yinzhi rides well.
facts.quote: He rode badly, with his weight too far back and the reins in the tips of his fingers, and had not slept since the noon before, and he let the hack follow hers.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: Tally and Wystan meet in person for the first time; Tally calls Yinzhi 'Qiu' and Wystan shows him the brass token and gives the name Ashmore.
facts.quote: Wystan took the brass out of his waistcoat and showed it on his palm before he gave the name.

facts.subject: Tally's notebook
facts.fact: Tally's oilcloth notebook, on a thong at his belt, logs every day since the letter with the same walk in the same order, 'North of the stone. Nothing.'; he shows it but does not let go of it.
facts.quote: He held it for Wystan to read and did not let go of it.

facts.subject: the last hind
facts.fact: The stone stands twenty-two paces north of the last carcass, a hind lying toward the stone.
facts.quote: He stopped with his toe against the stone.

facts.subject: the carcasses
facts.fact: The dead show no scavenging: eyes whole, a faint sweetish smell without rot; Wystan did not count them this chapter.
facts.quote: The eyes were whole.

facts.subject: the parish marker
facts.fact: The stone is a hip-high squared block of grey grit leaning west, yellow lichen on its north face, a surveyor's sighting groove on the dressed top; the south face bears TERM, the estate's name cut shallower and later, and an illegible line that may have been a year.
facts.quote: *TERM*, and the rest of a word the chancery still used, and under it the estate's name cut shallower, by somebody else, later.

facts.subject: the parish marker
facts.fact: Wystan touched the stone and felt nothing carried on it.
facts.quote: It had carried nothing that he could feel, and he had not thought it would.

facts.subject: the parish clerk
facts.fact: The parish clerk had the stone's before-the-roll dating from his father.
facts.quote: Parish clerk had it from his father.

facts.subject: the estate's round
facts.fact: The Ferriby estate's round comes up out of the birch from the south on the east side, meets the stone at its south-east corner and bends west along the estate's bound; north of the stone is parish ground.
facts.quote: Comes up out of their ground through the birch and goes along their bound, west.

facts.subject: Yinzhi
facts.fact: Yinzhi ran a fresh coil twice north of the stone and confirms the far side clean, as assay of record.
facts.quote: "Nothing," she said. "Clean."

facts.subject: the burn
facts.fact: Per Tally, the burn runs the foot of the timber down the whole cut and on north under the rise: the same water both sides of the stone; Wystan concludes it is not the burn.
facts.quote: So it was not the burn.

facts.subject: Tally
facts.fact: LIE: Tally says nothing is set out (troughs, anything filled) on his line or near it. He knows better; not true.
facts.quote: "Nothing set out on my line, nor near it."

facts.subject: the day book
facts.fact: Wystan records Tally's lie in the day book, attributed: 'Nothing set out, per Tally.'
facts.quote: *Burn, both sides of the stone. North side clean. Nothing set out, per Tally.*

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan stood eight divisions (twelfth to sixth) without food calling the scene late: swollen feet, cold shins, tremor, left calf knot, greying vision.
facts.quote: Eight divisions. He had counted every one.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: The working's price falls on the body, not the Crystal; a following-week debt is owed.
facts.quote: The week after would send its own bill.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Called Late reads, off the estate's round: somebody came up from the south, stopped well short of the stone, stood a while, went back the way he came, on foot at a walking pace, more than once.
facts.quote: "Somebody came up from the south," Wystan said.

facts.subject: the walker
facts.fact: The walker's passes lie layered with disagreeing clocks; the newest are weeks old and at least some broke ground the dead had already shed on; none went past the stopping place or followed the round west; nothing of him came near the stone. Wystan will not give a number.
facts.quote: The newest were weeks old.

facts.subject: the walker
facts.fact: Called Late cannot say who the walker is or what he did while standing.
facts.quote: "He stood," he said. "I cannot give you what he did standing."

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: MISREADING: Wystan concludes the walker turned short of the stone so the dead would lie on this side, i.e. the edge is a chosen line. Wrong: it is where an ordinary round stops.
facts.quote: He had turned short of the stone so that the dead would lie on this side of it.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: On turning Wystan faints briefly to one knee, bare palm flat on the stone; both calves cramp when he sits. Yinzhi and Tally witness it.
facts.quote: It did not go far.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: In the faint Wystan's bare palm touched the stone, his one lapse from holding things by the edge; he finds nothing on it.
facts.quote: He had not held it by the edge.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan finally eats Tally's bread, holding it by the crust's edge.
facts.quote: He took it by the edge of the crust, two fingers and a thumb.

facts.subject: the day book
facts.fact: Wystan writes the walker's sequence and the divisions against each pass in the day book, with 'stood, short of the stone; what, not had.'
facts.quote: He wrote the sequence in the plain words he had said it in, and the divisions against each pass as near as the field would give them, and under it, *stood, short of the stone; what, not had.*

facts.subject: the estate's round
facts.fact: Per Tally the round goes south round the whole estate, the estate's ground, not Tally's line.
facts.quote: It's theirs. It's not my line.

facts.subject: the fourth hind
facts.fact: The fourth hind's shoulder drew three times under Nuvalik's point: twice on her second day, once on her third, each smaller.
facts.quote: Twice on the second, once on the third.

facts.subject: the fourth hind
facts.fact: The fourth hind is finished now; Nuvalik found nothing in her on the morning of Day 5.
facts.quote: She is finished now.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik kept the contraction out of the book deliberately, so that no one would pour the hind again and lose what it was doing.
facts.quote: I did not write it down so that nobody could spend it.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas now knows of all three contractions and that Nuvalik held them back; Vesk and Foss heard it too.
facts.quote: Why is it not in the book," Malphas said.

facts.subject: the book
facts.fact: The contraction is entered in the project's book in Nuvalik's hand with the concealment dated: 'held back by me, three days, so that nobody could spend it'. It is the first entry that has her in it.
facts.quote: It was the first entry in the book in her hand that had her in it at all.

facts.subject: the eighth hind
facts.fact: Malphas orders the contraction reproduced: a drawing shoulder by the eighth division tomorrow (Day 6), under two different pairs of hands, recorded in the book by both.
facts.quote: By the eighth division tomorrow I want a shoulder that draws, and I want two hands on it that are not the same two hands, and I want it in the book in both.

facts.subject: Foss
facts.fact: Foss is to hold the eighth hind's joint while Nuvalik goes in, so he cannot be told he expected the draw.
facts.quote: He has the steadier hands and he has never had them in one, and if it comes in under his hand as well he cannot be told he expected it.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik has said aloud that the reproduction will not be as clean as the fourth hind.
facts.quote: It will not be as clean," she said.

facts.subject: the eighth hind
facts.fact: The eighth hind came off the rail hook at the fourth division of Day 5.
facts.quote: The eighth hind came down off the hook at the fourth division.

facts.subject: the eighth hind
facts.fact: The eighth hind was poured sealed at four places at the fourth hind's dilution, count of forty each, two hands, and written up in the book.
facts.quote: The small knocks went on while she wrote the eighth hind up in the ordinary way: four places, the count of forty, poured sealed, two hands.

facts.subject: the eighth hind
facts.fact: Because the sealed make-up tempers slower, the eighth hind is poured at the fifth division and stands a division less than the fourth before Nuvalik goes in; the book records it as a division less, not the same (figure rests on Vesk's lie).
facts.quote: If it tempers half a division slower, she is poured at the fifth division and not the fourth, and she stands a division less than the fourth hind did before I go in at her.

facts.subject: the field manual
facts.fact: Foss has a copy of the Division field manual: a grey limp-covered print taken off an issue, no number, name, chapter or mark of origin.
facts.quote: This is a print somebody took off an issue, badly, with the heads set by eye.

facts.subject: the field manual
facts.fact: Foss's print leads to nobody; its provenance runs through a chapter bench and a carter.
facts.quote: It came up the road in a carter's coat with four other books in the bundle, and the carrier could not have told you what any of them were.

facts.subject: the field manual
facts.fact: The manual is in about forty pockets in one district; a whole chapter bench has read it since the cut.
facts.quote: A whole chapter bench has been reading it since the cut, every man looking for the part about himself, and when a thing is in forty pockets in one district it stops being a thing you ask for and becomes a thing you decline.

facts.subject: Foss
facts.fact: Foss obtained the paragraph a season earlier than he had said.
facts.quote: I said a season and I was wrong by a season.

facts.subject: the field manual
facts.fact: The unsigned paragraph gives four ways attribution is broken: seal the object, interpose a hand, let a season pass, move a wall.
facts.quote: It is broken in four ways.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas had the fourth counter (move a wall) read twice and did nothing visible with it.
facts.quote: Read the last one again," Malphas said.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas spent two years designing against the paragraph from hearsay; three counters right, one backwards: he believed attribution ran up from object to hand, so the crew touched flasks bare. He puts the error in the book.
facts.quote: I have had you all touching flasks bare because I believed it ran the other way, up, from the object to the hand.

facts.subject: house rules
facts.fact: House rule one: every flask Fixatio-sealed when made up, seal broken only at the table, resealed over what is left; nothing tempers open.
facts.quote: First: every flask is Fixatio-sealed when it is made up, and the seal is not broken until the flask is at the table, and it goes on again over what is left.

facts.subject: house rules
facts.fact: House rule two: no live dose touched bare; gloves on before the seal comes off; gloves stay in the room.
facts.quote: Second: no live dose is touched bare.

facts.subject: house rules
facts.fact: House rule three: nothing from a flask or the substrate reaches Malphas without a second pair of hands; Vesk makes up, Nuvalik or Foss carries, Nuvalik cuts; Malphas touches neither dose nor substrate.
facts.quote: Third: nothing comes from a flask to me, or from the substrate to me, without a second pair of hands between.

facts.subject: house rules
facts.fact: The season and the wall are not house rules but the end of the work; written under the three with a rule across.
facts.quote: Write them both under the three and put a rule across, so the two do not read as instructions.

facts.subject: house rules
facts.fact: Foss cuts the three rules into a board for the door, since ink on a coldhouse door would not last a turn.
facts.quote: Behind her Foss was cutting the three rules into a board with a knife.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Malphas put his hand on the poured ninth hind's flank on the first night; he calls it a bad habit that stops now.
facts.quote: You put your hand on the ninth hind's flank on the first night.

facts.subject: Foss
facts.fact: Malphas promises Foss release under his own name when the work is done, and not to ask or send anyone after; it goes in the book.
facts.quote: When the work is done you will be released with your own name.

facts.subject: Foss
facts.fact: Foss's given name is Ilmar.
facts.quote: Ilmar Foss, on a bench, with hands.

facts.subject: Foss
facts.fact: Foss held a numbered instrument for eleven years and was struck off for a rounding convention.
facts.quote: I held a numbered instrument for eleven years.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk claims the dilution can be tempered sealed, half a division slower. He has never done it and does not know.
facts.quote: "It can be tempered sealed," he said.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: The sealed make-up took longer than it ever had, and nobody remarked on it.
facts.quote: Then he made the dilution up inside the flask with the seal on, and it took longer than it had ever taken, and nobody said anything about that either.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk wears the yard gloves, canvas, the only pair in the building; his hands do not close fully in them.
facts.quote: They were the yard gloves, canvas, stiff with the cold, the only pair in the building, and he stood a long moment with his hands in them and his hands not closing all the way.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk's two ridged yellow graft nails have grown out again since the fourth day.
facts.quote: The two nails on the fingers that had taken stood up over the edge of the bench, ridged and yellow and grown out again since the fourth day, and he was looking at them the way she looked at a joint she did not like.

facts.subject: Vesk
facts.fact: Vesk has had all nine hinds through his hands and nothing like the contraction from any other.
facts.quote: I have had nothing like it off any of the others and I have had all nine of them through my hands.

facts.subject: Malphas
facts.fact: Nuvalik sees Malphas's hands keep a living colour at four degrees while hers go the colour of tallow.
facts.quote: The gauge over the door had stood at four degrees since the first division and her own fingers had gone the colour of tallow inside the first quarter of it, the way they did every day, and his were the colour of hands.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik believes Malphas's hands keep colour because he comes from a warm building and sits only a division; she has no control case.
facts.quote: He came from a warm building, and he sat a division, and he went back to a warm building, and a division was not long enough to take the colour out of a man who was not working in it.

facts.subject: the ice-press room
facts.fact: The ice-press room has had no hum (no main) for four years.
facts.quote: It had not had one for four years.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: The ninth hind, under sacking since the first night, has done nothing; nothing written on her in three days.
facts.quote: Nuvalik had written nothing about her in three days because there had been nothing to write.

facts.subject: the ninth hind
facts.fact: At chapter end Nuvalik takes the big knife to open the ninth hind.
facts.quote: She went back in and took the big knife off the hook to start the ninth hind's hide off her, because a hind that had done nothing in five days was a hind you learned from by opening.

facts.subject: Nuvalik
facts.fact: Nuvalik sees nothing to be released to: her name was carried by three before her and spent in this room.
facts.quote: There was nothing to release her to.

facts.subject: Josse Garretsohn
facts.fact: The lick-keeper of the Ferriby estate's round is Josse Garretsohn; first seen ch7.
facts.quote: Josse Garretsohn.

facts.subject: the lick round
facts.fact: The Ferriby round runs north from the home farm to the birch with a salt lick every half mile on knee-high squared oak posts.
facts.quote: A lick every half mile.

facts.subject: the lick round
facts.fact: The round turns at the birch, as Josse's father's did; past the birch it goes along the bound by the old stone, with no beasts worth the salt.
facts.quote: My father turned at the birch. I turn at the birch.

facts.subject: tonic blocks
facts.fact: The blocks are new tonic blocks this season: grey salt with a rust-brown streak poured through at a slant, the size of an assize loaf; before this season the licks held plain white salt.
facts.quote: New this season.

facts.subject: tonic blocks
facts.fact: The steward paid for the tonic blocks, notched on a split hazel tally with a nicked notch for tonic: the steward's money, not the farm's.
facts.quote: Tonic's his money, not the farm's.

facts.subject: Josse Garretsohn
facts.fact: LIE (uncorrected; Wystan believes it): Josse says the blocks come from the steward's barn at the home farm and he loads there. Per the ch8 outline, a carter supplies him.
facts.quote: Steward keeps them in the barn, I load up there.

facts.subject: Josse Garretsohn
facts.fact: Josse refuses to hand over his half of the tally to anyone, the Register included.
facts.quote: Not to the steward, not to the Register, not to anybody, that's what a half is.

facts.subject: Josse Garretsohn
facts.fact: Josse says no one has walked the round with him since the tonic, and the steward (bad hip) has never been up past the second field.
facts.quote: The steward's never been up past the second field in his life, he's got a bad hip, he'd...

facts.subject: Josse Garretsohn
facts.fact: Josse knows the Register is taking the steward's block from the birch lick; he has seen the brass but has no name, only 'the Register'.
facts.quote: Register, then.

facts.subject: Josse Garretsohn
facts.fact: Josse set the birch lick's block before the thaw (weeks back).
facts.quote: Set a new one there back before the thaw came in.

facts.subject: the last lick
facts.fact: The last lick is just inside the birch on the east side, in a hollow out of sight of the cut; no post beyond it toward the stone's south-east corner. It is Called Late's stopping place.
facts.quote: There was no post on it after this one.

facts.subject: the far side of the marker
facts.fact: The far side of the marker stone is clean because the salt round stopped at the birch and the carrier turned home there.
facts.quote: The man who carried the salt had put his frame on his back here and gone home down the same road, and the far side of the marker stone was clean because nobody had ever carried any salt to it.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan now knows his ch5 reading (the walker turned short of the stone to keep the dead on this side) was wrong: the walker turned because it was the last post.
facts.quote: He had turned because this was the last post.

facts.subject: the birch hollow
facts.fact: Red-brown hind hair is rubbed into the bark at hind-shoulder height on the north faces of the birches round the last lick, through to the green on one; Wystan records it uninterpreted.
facts.quote: He could not say what a beast did that for, at a lick, facing away from the salt.

facts.subject: the birch block
facts.fact: Yinzhi's coil browned along its length on the birch block: it carried a working (assay of record: carrying).
facts.quote: "It's carrying," she said.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan grips the birch block bare-handed with his right hand, deliberately; Yinzhi witnesses it.
facts.quote: He did not take the block by the edge.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Salt entered the ink-cracks at the nails of Wystan's right palm; stinging went to a steady burn and he did not wipe it.
facts.quote: The cracks at the nails had gone from stinging to a steady burn.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: Wystan's left calf still carries the knot from the night at the stone.
facts.quote: The left calf caught and let go.

facts.subject: the forty-third minute
facts.fact: The Hand gave the forty-third minute: Josse setting the birch block, content, nobody else in it, turning south for home.
facts.quote: There was nobody else anywhere in it.

facts.subject: the forty-third minute
facts.fact: The minute is entered as the forty-third at the back of the day book under Keld's (forty-one more, forty-two with Keld's), with the word 'content'.
facts.quote: Under it were forty-one more, forty-two with Keld's, the newest a hind in the North Ferriby cut.

facts.subject: Wystan
facts.fact: MISREADING (uncorrected): from a minute with nobody else in it, Wystan concludes the formulator never goes near the beasts.
facts.quote: A man who put his dose into salt and let other hands carry it out to the beasts was a man who never went near them.

facts.subject: the birch block
facts.fact: The birch block is tinned in the widest tin (the soil tin), sealed with brass wax and struck with Wystan's brass; entered in the Register file Ferriby.
facts.quote: He took out the brass wax and warmed the stick in his fist, the left fist, and ran the wax round the join, and struck his brass into it while it was soft.

hooks.text: Tally found clean ground on the far side of the parish marker, twenty-two paces past the last carcass, and checked it twice; Wystan writes 'ask Tally who set the marker'. Paid when the lick-keeper's round is found to end at the marker: the carrier turned home there.

events.what: Wystan's letter asks Tally who set the parish marker and what the animals on the line drank from; Tally's clean far side, checked twice.
events.quote: Tell me who set the parish marker on the Ferriby line, and when, if anybody knows.

events.what: Tally's letter identifies the marker as the Ferriby estate's old survey stone; Called Late reads a walker on the estate's round turning short of it, more than once; Wystan writes 'the round.'
events.quote: It is the Ferriby estate's old survey stone, the corner of their ground, set by the estate before the parish was on the roll.

events.what: The round ends at the last lick in the birch; the carrier turned home there, so the far side of the marker is clean.
events.quote: The salt stopped here.

hooks.text: A quarter inch of new growth inside a Fixatio-anchored tin with the seal unbroken; the day book reads 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'. Paid at the hearing: Fixatio held what it was given, and what it was given was a running working.

events.what: A quarter inch of new growth under an unbroken Fixatio seal, logged 'crown +¼ in sealed, 11d'.
events.quote: Something in the tin had gone on running under a seal that was sold to the courts as a promise that nothing would.

hooks.text: 'They are chapter wax and I will want them later.' Four pieces of the broken seal, dated and kept. Paid at the hearing: the pieces fit the join and prove custody.

events.what: Four pieces of chapter wax fit the join, folded and dated for custody.
events.quote: The day somebody wants to say this tin was opened on the road, I want four pieces of chapter wax that fit a join, and a paper round them dated before anybody asked.

hooks.text: Wystan asks Tally to keep walking and measuring: 'I want a second dataset from the same observer.' Paid when the notebook is taken from Tally's walking body, complete to the night he died.

events.what: Wystan asks Tally for a notebook kept on his person: a second dataset from the same observer.
events.quote: I want a second dataset from the same observer.

events.what: Tally shows the notebook kept daily since the letter, 'North of the stone. Nothing.', without letting go of it.
events.quote: Tally took the notebook off its thong and opened it.

hooks.text: The bulletin clerk told Tally the Night Register was a person. The cell knows its hunter only as the Night Register. Paid when the Register is folded and Malphas closes the line.

events.what: The bulletin clerk told Tally the Night Register was a person; one line in a minute could fold the desk.
events.quote: A desk could be folded into another desk by one line in a Prime Warden's minute.

events.what: Wystan gives Josse only 'the Register', no name.
events.quote: Register, then.

hooks.text: Wystan holds everything by the very edge, two-fingered, even a cup. Paid in VI: Salter sees a man holding a cup that way across the quad, notes it, and nothing follows.

events.what: Wystan holds his tea by the rim, thumb and two fingers, away from his palm.
events.quote: He gave her one and took the other to the window, and he held it there by the rim, the thumb on one side and two fingers on the other, so that none of the heat came near his palm.

events.what: Wystan breaks the edge habit to grip the block bare; bread by the crust edge, tin by its rim.
events.quote: He did not take the block by the edge.

hooks.text: Malphas's hands keep a living man's colour in a four-degree coldhouse. Paid in the hearing gallery, at the verdict, as a detail Wystan notices and never explains; never recognition.

events.what: Malphas's fingers keep a living man's colour after sitting ungloved at four degrees; Vesk explains it away by the press.
events.quote: What there was instead was the one thing Vesk could not get past: the Lord had been sitting on an iron bench in a room the housing gauge had at four degrees since the first division, with no gloves on and his coat folded beside him and not under him, and his fingers were the colour of a living man's fingers.

events.what: Nuvalik sees his hands keep their colour at four degrees and explains it by his warm building (her misreading).
events.quote: He came from a warm building, and he sat a division, and he went back to a warm building, and a division was not long enough to take the colour out of a man who was not working in it.

hooks.text: Nuvalik got contraction out of the fourth hind's shoulder twice and did not report it; Malphas 'will discuss with her separately'. Paid when the discussion happens.

events.what: Vesk asks about the fourth hind's twice-reported contraction; Nuvalik says it is all written down.
events.quote: Everything the fourth hind gave me is written down.

events.what: Malphas takes up the concealed contraction; Nuvalik gives it as three, says why she held it back; entered in the book with the concealment dated and ordered reproduced under witness.
events.quote: I did not write it down so that nobody could spend it.

hooks.text: Nuvalik carries a name three people carried before her and thinks she has spent all three on this work. Paid when she sets down the name she wears in the cell and leaves; she does not inform.

events.what: Nuvalik tells Vesk her name was worn by three before her and she has spent all three in this room.
events.quote: The name I wear was worn by three people before me.

events.what: Set beside Foss's release: Nuvalik has nothing to be released to; the name is spent.
events.quote: A name was not a coat.

hooks.text: Vesk's grafted fingers, the ridged yellow nails that will not stop growing; the village that put stones on its graves. Paid when he dies of his own formulation and Nuvalik lays stones on his walking body.

events.what: Vesk's two grafts and ridged yellow nails; his village's nine grave stones.
events.quote: The second had taken in the way that a thing takes when it has been asked twice, which was well enough for holding and badly for gripping, and the nails on the two fingers that took had come in ridged and yellow and had never stopped growing since.

events.what: No live dose touched bare; the graft nails grown out again; the only gloves on hands that close two thirds.
events.quote: The two nails on the fingers that had taken stood up over the edge of the bench, ridged and yellow and grown out again since the fourth day, and he was looking at them the way she looked at a joint she did not like.

hooks.text: 'Where I was raised, the sky finishes what the ground starts, and when the sky refuses, people walk out to see why.' Paid when the ravens will not come down to Tally and he walks.

events.what: Nuvalik gives the saying about the sky finishing what the ground starts.
events.quote: Where I was raised, the sky finishes what the ground starts, and when the sky refuses, people walk out to see why.

hooks.text: Keld's minute, taken off a door handle, lucid, waiting for relief; checked every morning against a written record. It slips by a word after Cutler Row; paid when it is set right at Keld's bedside.

events.what: Keld's minute checked against the written record; it has not moved; relief came late.
events.quote: It had not moved.

events.what: Keld's stays at the head of the column as the forty-third is entered.
events.quote: Keld's stood at the head of the column, where it always stood.

hooks.text: Wystan's Shell rests near zero saturation; free residue in a closed volume runs toward him. The dead lean to the quiet. He believes they are being sent to him; paid when he learns he is the sink and nobody sent them.

events.what: Residue settles on Wystan in Lyle's shut room; he misreads it as falling on everyone.
events.quote: It began on the backs of his hands first, as it always did, where the stain was.

hooks.text: The Register token is brass, not silver, because the Night Register is not a full desk, and he has never asked to have it changed. Paid when he hands it in.

events.what: Brass token explained against silver; carried four years, never asked to change it.
events.quote: The Register's token was brass because the Night Register was not a full desk.

events.what: The brass is shown before any name at the start of the conversation.
events.quote: Wystan took the brass out of his waistcoat and showed it on his palm.

hooks.text: Suppression held waking and sleeping; six people alive know what Stage he is. Paid when he drops it in the death-house and the whole cordon knows.

events.what: Six people alive know his Stage; Lyle is one of them.
events.quote: *Six people alive know what Stage I hold.*

hooks.text: Deming: thirty-one days of usefulness left, and Malphas has already counted them. Paid on the thirty-first day.

events.what: Deming privately counts thirty-one days of usefulness on the almanac and knows Malphas counted them first.
events.quote: Thirty-one days of a man who held the contract, and the pen, and the chop, and was useful.

hooks.text: 'In eleven weeks somebody in a room in the capital will look at the Swale line and see a bad spring.' Paid when the Logistics return publishes.

events.what: Deming tells the factor the capital will see a bad spring in eleven weeks, from his own derivation off the house's copies, and has it noted in the factor's book.
events.quote: In eleven weeks somebody in a room in the capital will look at the Swale line and see a bad spring.

hooks.text: 'I would prefer the file be built off a word I chose.' Every letter names Project Zombification. Paid when the Bench titles the file by the word and every thread ends in it.

events.what: The covering letter's second line names Project Zombification on Malphas's order ('a word I chose'); the factor marks it and files it apart, lying that it goes in the stove.
events.quote: On the account of Project Zombification, second tranche.

hooks.text: 'That is how they found the Hollow Shaft people. They found a name in a private correspondence.' Paid when the precedent is read into the record at Deming's hearing.

events.what: Deming tells the Hollow Shaft story to the factor as a joke about careless men, thumb going round the hat brim.
events.quote: That is how they found the Hollow Shaft people.

hooks.text: Foss reads the Division field manual's unsigned paragraph on anamnetic reading and its counters; Malphas adopts them as house rules. Paid when a moved wall makes Wystan's Called Late at Greyshaft Nine confidently wrong.

events.what: Foss reads the unsigned field-manual paragraph; Malphas has the wall counter read twice, adopts three counters as house rules and rules the season and wall off as the work's end.
events.quote: Move a wall, and the attribution is read against a room that is not the room.

hooks.text: 'The ninth hind is the freshest and she is the one I want.' Paid when she stands up off the table and leans to the standpipe.

events.what: The ninth hind on the table with the matrix pour in her; she does not stand, the hide draws up once.
events.quote: The ninth hind is the freshest and she is the one I want.

events.what: The ninth hind has done nothing in five days; Nuvalik takes the big knife to open her.
events.quote: The hide over the scapula lay the way hide lies.

hooks.text: Foss pays the carter in salt bars because salt bars leave no bill; the salt bar is money that can be eaten. Paid when the parish dead walk out of the pit with the bars in their purses.
Wystan's margin note: edges. Paid when the walkers erase them and he strikes the word in public.

events.what: Wystan writes 'edges' in the docket-book margin level with Brack's line.
events.quote: In the margin, level with Brack's line, he wrote one word.

events.what: Lyle reads 'edges' in the margin; the position goes into her minute.
events.quote: She read *edges* and the plain sentences underneath it, and then *A dose goes where it is put*, and took up her pen, and copied the line into the minute in a small upright hand, and wrote the date and the division beside it.

events.what: Wystan reads the walker's turn as a chosen edge; the margin grows to 'the estate. before the roll.' and 'the round.'
events.quote: That was the edge.

events.what: The margin grows 'the round's end. the last lick. the birch.'; edges reinforced, not struck.
events.quote: The dose had gone where it was put.

hooks.text: Brack's classification: Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, no operator indicated, correct off a true measurement. Paid when the Accord's official classification stays bleed and Brack signs it again.

events.what: Brack's Bureau return in the docket book: bleed, no operator, no file; closed.
events.quote: A day clerk had entered it in the copying hand, the Bureau's return pinned to the leaf beside it, signed in its own ink: *Wellspring bleed, Verdantia, tertiary expression, no operator indicated. No further action. No file. E. Brack, Lattice Classification Bureau, northern office.*

events.what: Brack stands by bleed and says he would sign it again.
events.quote: I'd sign it again this afternoon.

hooks.text: STAY's counter: threaten something outside the boundary; two Enforcement men have used it. Harrow is one. Paid when Wystan drops STAY to save the family on the stair.
Article XX: a death-house may not be cut; the exemption is claimed far more often than granted. Paid when Wystan holds the Wicket death-house under STAY and the dead are entered on the roll.
Deming decides that whatever the Accord asks he will not give it the hand. Paid when the Ruling chair asks and he refuses under reservation.
Malphas promises Foss release with his own name when the work is done. Paid when Foss takes a bench under his own name and informs no one.

events.what: Malphas promises Foss release under his own name when the work is done; Foss says it is not in his gift; it goes in the book.
events.quote: When the work is done you will be released with your own name.

hooks.text: When the Bench reserves the hand, the exhibits return to the filing party: the Ferriby tin and the chapter wax go back to Timberline. Paid when the tin is the lesson at Aetherion.

The Society tells Wystan the academies ask for field instruction; at Aetherion, Mu-jin has promised Class X the Night's Watch for 'field work, real cases'. Paid when Wystan takes the class to a real case.
At the Aetherion the hum stops at one door, the west range; Wystan stands there and turns back east. Paid when he does it again at the end of the week and goes no further.
His technique gets the hand, never the purse; Article XV prosecutes only the purse. This case inverts it. Paid when he teaches it: the hand or the purse, never both.

events.what: Wystan tells Brack he will get a hand and not a purse; Brack answers that Fifteen wants the purse.
events.quote: "I will get a hand and not a purse."

events.what: The Hand gives Wystan the lick-keeper's hand, not the formulator's.
events.quote: It was the wrong one.

summaries.title: The Docket Head
summaries.summary: Wystan checks and blots Yinzhi's full name at the docket head and enters her as assay of record. Gloved, he moves the Ferriby wedge with forceps into a fresh Division Fixatio tin, seals it with brass wax and strikes his brass into the seal. He logs it in the day book as Register file Ferriby, exhibit one, "crown +¼ in sealed." He collects the four pieces of chapter wax. He folds them in a druggist's paper, dated, for custody. Over grounding tea he asks whether the bracelet is still pulling, and Yinzhi says no. He rejects a nine-word wire and writes Tally a letter: walk the line and measure into a notebook, a second dataset from the same observer, who set the marker, and what the animals put their mouths to. He signs it "Night Register, Cutler Row." He enters the Register's position, "A dose goes where it is put," and records the forty-second minute. The main returns at the sixth division. At the day desk he writes his memorandum under Brack's closed classification, with *edges* in the margin. A day clerk reads only the classification and shelves the book.

summaries.title: Twenty-Two Drops
summaries.summary: Day one, the second division to the ninth, at Greyshaft Nine. Nuvalik brings the ninth hind down off the rail onto the slate table. Vesk has built the contractile matrix into the third-dilution formulation on one pour and lets it stand, then carries the flask in both palms and works it in at four places along the near flank, the count of forty between each. The colour clears inland, faster at the two forward pours; Foss, at the glass, gives the reason (the trunk quit last, the forward channel is finest, the finest channel pulls hardest) and calls the synthesis filthy and correct, wanting both findings in the book. Malphas asks Foss to get the Arbitration Division's field manual for its unsigned attribution paragraph; Foss refuses a wire and says it will take a season, and Malphas accepts a season. Nuvalik states what the hind is: no Crystal, no self, a net that shortens toward the emptier end. Malphas orders the night written up in ink under the project's name by four hands. The hind does not stand. Vesk sees the hide at her shoulder draw up once, tells nobody, and counts the drip to twenty-two.

summaries.title: The Morning Check
summaries.summary: Day 1, noon to the ninth division. Wystan wakes with his hands shaking. He recalls Keld's minute, then reads the written record against it word for word. It has not moved. At the medical house the porter admits him by his face, because his brass is on the tin lid at Cutler Row. Keld sits at the window counting under his breath at something Wystan cannot find. He asks "Is that them" and says "They said the sixth." At the day desk Prime Warden Elspeth Lyle reads the edges memorandum and calls the file a curiosity. The Register may keep it open until the quarterly inspection of the gauge-housing and not a day longer. In the upper passage Brack stands by bleed and hands over the Bureau's raw Ferriby field sheets unasked. In Lyle's shut room the position and the term go into her minute in ink, under her silver, and he initials both. Residue settles on his skin and he does not remark it. Lyle orders the sheets entered as received unasked and denies sending for Brack. At the ninth division Wystan tells Brack: "I will get a hand and not a purse."

summaries.title: A Number in the Room
summaries.summary: Day 2, fourth to sixth division, Xu counting house. Deming enters the second tranche of the Swale supply as wastage at the array, where four years of the column had run flat. He writes the covering letter in the house form. Its second line reads "On the account of Project Zombification, second tranche", as Malphas ordered against his argument. The cause given is "the thaw", signed for the house under the Xu chop. On the almanac he privately counts thirty-one days of usefulness and knows Malphas counted them first. He derives eleven weeks to the Logistics return from the house's own copies. The Logistics factor, unnamed, queries the step in the column and pushes to move the loss into carriage on the house's bond. Deming holds it to wastage. He tells the factor that in eleven weeks the capital will see "a bad spring", and has it noted in the factor's pocket-book with the division. The factor reads the letter's second line twice and makes an unexplained hooked mark beside it. He files it between boards, says covering letters go in the stove, and leaves upriver with it after Deming tells the Hollow Shaft story as a joke.

summaries.title: Who Set the Marker
summaries.summary: Day 4, sixth division, to Day 5, sixth. Yinzhi brings the Society's bundle to Cutler Row. Tally's letter: he walks daily again; the marker is the Ferriby estate's old survey stone, their corner, set before the parish was on the roll. It leaves the second question unanswered. Wystan wires the Timberline bench and rides out with Yinzhi on hacks charged to Lyle's bill. At the eleventh division Tally, first seen, shows his notebook without letting go of it and walks them the line. The stone bears a weathered *TERM* and the estate's name. The estate's round comes up through the birch, meets the stone and bends west. Yinzhi's coil confirms the far side clean. Tally says the burn runs both sides and lies that nothing is set out. Wystan stands eight divisions without food and calls the scene late. At the sixth he states: somebody came up from the south along the estate's round, stopped short of the stone, stood a while, and went back the way he came, on foot, at a walking pace, more than once. What he did standing cannot be read. Wystan faints briefly, eats, writes *the round* in the margin, and looks down it.

summaries.title: Separately
summaries.summary: Day 5, third to eighth division, Greyshaft Nine ice-press room. Malphas takes up Nuvalik's ch2 line that everything the fourth hind gave her is written down, against the book's three entries. She admits the shoulder drew three times under her point — twice on the hind's second day, once on her third, each smaller, now finished — and says she kept it out of the book because a thing that twitches is a thing that will walk and a pour would have lost it. Malphas orders it entered in her hand with the concealment dated, and orders it reproduced by the eighth division tomorrow under two hands: the eighth hind down, poured at the fourth's dilution, Foss holding the joint. Foss produces a nameless print of the Division field manual a season early and reads the unsigned paragraph: seal the object, interpose a hand, wait a season, move a wall. Malphas makes the first three house rules (Fixatio seal, no live dose bare, everything through a second pair of hands), leaves the season and the wall as the work's end, and promises Foss release under his own name. The eighth hind is poured sealed. The ninth has done nothing.

summaries.title: The Lick-Keeper
summaries.summary: Day 7. Wystan and Yinzhi walk the Ferriby estate's round north from the home farm. There is a salt lick every half mile, on knee-high oak posts, and the blocks are new tonic blocks, grey with a brown streak. At one post they meet the lick-keeper Josse Garretsohn, first seen, setting blocks bare-handed. Wystan shows the brass and gives only "the Register". Josse says the round turns at the birch, as his father's did, and that the steward paid for the tonic on the split tally. He lies that the blocks come from the home-farm barn and refuses to hand over his half of the tally. He set the birch lick before the thaw. The last lick is inside the birch on the east side, well short of the stone. It sits at Called Late's stopping place: the salt stopped there and the carrier turned home. Hair is rubbed into the bark on the north faces of the trunks round it. Yinzhi's coil shows the block carrying. Wystan grips it bare-handed and takes the forty-third minute: Josse setting it, content, nobody else in it. He concludes the formulator never goes near them. The block is tinned under his brass.
